decisions.reason: This product line sits squarely in the firm's core geospatial integration business and its continued clear positioning suggests results are at or near aspiration levels, so management would retain it.

The digital twin service matches the firm's long-term direction, but its limited visibility and still-uncertain demand likely leave it below fully satisfactory aspirations, so it is kept under close review rather than dropped immediately.

Because this identity-related service appears less distinctive than the firm's GIS-specific access offering and likely faces aspiration shortfalls relative to internal alternatives, management would reallocate its resources elsewhere.
The GIS-focused identity and access service directly complements the firm's enterprise GeoIT solutions and likely performs well enough relative to aspirations to justify continued support.
This workshop builds directly on the firm's consulting, training, and process-integration strengths and likely requires little slack to sustain, so management would keep it while demand develops.
